callouts.text:
28 USD DECLINE IN 2H20
THE MOVE IT EXISTS TO CATCH

points: Stop-and-reverse: the strategy is never flat. Ten signals in four hours alternating short-long-short-long without exception — each entry closes the previous position and opens the opposite one.
Average time in a direction is 23 minutes. Three of the flips lasted 12, 8 and 5 minutes (2→3, 4→5, 6→7) — all of them inside or entering the chop box, which is where a channel system bleeds.

The 28 USD slide from 17:00 to 19:20 is the move a channel breakout exists to catch. It held short for the first leg, then flipped long at 4,358 and 4,356 mid-decline (entries 2 and 4) — buying bounces against a falling channel.

Gold is a genuinely better venue than EURUSD: 1m bars run ~2.6× larger relative to price (1.10 bp vs 0.42 bp) and the spread is roughly half in bp, so spread eats ~63% of a bar here against 333%. Still far from the <10% a breakout system needs — at 0.30 spread, 10 flips a day is ~20 USD against gold's ~55 USD range.
summary.bias: Verdict: NEVER FLAT, FLIPPING EVERY 23 MINUTES
